name: MA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district (D+15 PVI) with incumbent Stephen Lynch running
Lynch has a large financial advantage; Republican Burke raised only ~$1,500 with negative cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
No competitive polling or expert ratings signal vulnerability
model.rationale: Lynch holds a D+15 district with incumbency and a massive fundraising edge, while Burke's campaign is essentially unfunded. Markets price this at 97% Democratic, consistent with fundamentals pointing to a Safe D hold.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or scandal shifting the fundamentals is the only realistic path to movement here.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Stephen Lynch seeks another term in a Boston-area district that leans Democratic by 15 points, and he enters the general election after easily securing renomination. His campaign has raised over $900,000 and holds more than $640,000 on hand, while Republican Robert Burke has raised roughly $1,500 and reports negative cash. Outside groups have spent modestly against Lynch, but nothing suggests a serious challenge.

Prediction markets give Lynch about a 97% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
